title: SPF basics
caption: Sunscreen in the UAE isn't just a beach habit — UV radiation here is strong enough to trigger pigmentation year-round, even through car windows and on overcast days. Two types of UV matter: UVB burns the surface and drives tanning, while UVA penetrates deeper and is the main driver of dark spots, uneven skin tone, and accelerated skin ageing. Both are present at full intensity in a Dubai summer. SPF numbers only measure UVB protection. To cover UVA too, the label needs to say 'broad spectrum' — that's the phrase to look for, not just a high SPF number. Texture matters more than most guides admit. Dubai's heat and AC cycling breaks down certain formulas faster, causes pilling under makeup, and makes heavy creams feel suffocating. Mineral filters (zinc oxide, titanium dioxide) sit on the surface and are generally better tolerated on darker skin tones, which are more prone to post-inflammatory pigmentation from sun exposure. Chemical filters absorb UV energy — effective, but some cause sensitivity, especially in high-heat conditions. Reapplication every two hours outdoors is the mechanism that makes sunscreen work, not just the morning application. Not medical advice, just the honest basics. Learn more at cliniclick.ae/concerns/pigmentation/what-is-pigmentation
